newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Committee in Bahrain for talks on row with Qatar.
newsitem.headline: Committee in Bahrain for talks on row with Qatar.

text.p: Foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman and the United Arab Emirates held talks in Bahrain as part of efforts to improve ties between Bahrain and Qatar strained by a territorial row.

The official Gulf News Agency said the committee of four foreign ministers met Bahrain's Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammad bin Mubarak al-Khalifa on Sunday night shortly after arriving in Manama from talks in Qatar.
The mediation committee earlier on Sunday met Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani in Doha.

The committee, set up by a Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit in December, had failed to convince the two countries to agree to a memorandum of understanding during two meetings in Riyadh earlier this month, Gulf Arab officials said.
Arab diplomats said the committee might introduce some amendments to the document to narrow differences between Bahrain and Qatar, who along with the four other countries form the GCC.
Qatar and Bahrain have been locked for decades in a dispute over a cluster of islands, sandbanks and reefs in the Gulf, controlled by Manama since the 1930s, but also claimed by Doha.
Doha took the dispute to the International Court of Justice at The Hague in 1991, a move opposed by Manama which insists on a regional solution.
Ties were further strained after Bahrain accused two Qataris of spying -- which Doha denied -- and boycotted the GCC summit in Qatar. Bahrain later pardoned the two Qataris.
Qatari officials told Reuters some of Qatar's plans to mend fences included:
- A halt to Bahraini media campaigns against Doha -- which have eased over the last weeks.

- A ban on any new construction on the disputed islands and a declaration that all past construction work is null and void. Bahrain has built a coast guard station on the Fash ad-Dibal, a coral reef mid-way between both states and a tourism resort on Hawar island over the past years.

- Not to allow any group to use each other's soil to work against the security of the other or to shelter groups that undermine the security of the other state. Qatar wants Bahrain to hand over several people it has accused of taking part in last year's failed plot to topple the government. Bahrain denies that.
